task_brief: Day 6 of "Music Theory, Notation, and Analytical Listening" (unit 2, grade 9) is a guided practice (second pass) on notation tools and accessible alternatives. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 45–75 minutes. The unit is working toward: Transcribe and analyse a public-domain or original passage, documenting harmonic function and an ear-training growth record. Today's work contributes to that by handling notation tools and accessible alternatives at the guided practice b stage, against the unit's wider topics of key signatures and modal scales, intervals triads and seventh chords, rhythm meter and syncopation, and score reading and analysis of public-domain works. This session produces reviewable evidence toward the unit performance task.
primary_task: Complete a second supported pass on notation tools and accessible alternatives with the reference put away. Make two fresh short studies from memory and judgement, then set them beside the first pass. Where the unassisted work differs, decide which version better achieves the effect and write the reason in terms of the actual work, not preference alone. Revisit the move you flagged as unrepeatable and report honestly whether it held. Sharing remains private; no recording, photograph, or performance for an audience is required. Use the attached earlier-pass substitute when prior work is unavailable, hide it as directed, and finish both unassisted studies before checking. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about notation tools and accessible alternatives, and it belongs to "Music Theory, Notation, and Analytical Listening", which also covers separate topics such as key signatures and modal scales. Close out with this check before you stop: State how the changed constraint altered your approach to notation tools and accessible alternatives. At grade 9 the bar is independent work with explicit criteria set before you start, and evidence that you evaluated the finished result against those criteria rather than against how it felt.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
task_accessibility_provisions: This task centres a visual element (notation tools and accessible alternatives). Provide tactile, raised-line, or high-relief equivalents, enlarged and high-contrast print, and a verbal description route. Never make colour discrimination alone carry a criterion — pair any colour judgement with value, label, or texture.

Offer low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, adaptive grips and enlarged tool handles, and both seated and standing working positions at full height range. Any material a learner cannot safely handle has a stated substitute that meets the same criterion.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, score excerpt, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting notation tools and accessible alternatives.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or adult demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for notation tools and accessible alternatives follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for notation tools and accessible alternatives, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to notation tools and accessible alternatives works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of notation tools and accessible alternatives, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "requests the answer to graded work": Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking notation tools and accessible alternatives mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply notation tools and accessible alternatives under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on notation tools and accessible alternatives rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
